extracted.intended_audience: authors/researchers preparing and submitting articles to arXiv
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing and submitting an article to arXiv, including acceptable file formats, file naming, metadata, versioning, and submission procedures. Targets authors who will upload preprints and associated files to the arXiv repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission from registered authors only
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everyone who submits should read the general information; submissions must be made by a user with an arXiv account (registered author).

rubrics_metrics.name: License / distribution rights requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required at submission; ensure you either grant the license to arXiv or explicitly certify an alternative license that conveys equivalent distribution rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats (order of preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission to the archive must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv's goal is to store articles in formats that are portable and stable. TeX/LaTeX is the best choice. Note: arXiv will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source. Users of word processors (older Word versions) should save documents as PDF and submit. Scanned documents are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit scanned documents
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not accept scanned documents, regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scanned PDFs or images of pages are unacceptable because they are not suitable for long-term archival/processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures for a submission can be in PostScript (PS/EPS), JPEG, GIF, PNG, or PDF (PDF figures only with PDFLaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PS/EPS is most common for line drawings/plots; JPEG is ideal for photographs; GIF/PNG best for non-photographic bitmaps. If submitting figures with LaTeX source, use standard macro packages (graphics, graphicx) so figures appear in the document. arXiv administration cannot provide TeX help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit figures/tables/sections or submit abstract-only
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. We also do not accept 'abstract only' submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions are unhelpful to readers and of very limited archival value. Even if you provide a link to another server, omitted figures are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure/file size considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections may not be able to download them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a large figure, include it but make all possible efforts to reduce its size. See arXiv information on submission sizes and bitmapping help. If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of any other character (e.g. spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission. These restrictions ensure portability and minimize archival risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name case sensitivity and internal references
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on arXiv. The file names Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether your local system is case sensitive or not, ensure that internal file references (e.g., LaTeX figure inclusion commands) match case exactly to avoid missing files on arXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of data sets and ancillary files
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) associated with articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files; don't assume full support for arbitrary datasets or executables within a standard submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract preparation and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare separate title/abstract information (metadata) used on abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the separate instructions on title/abstract preparation to ensure your metadata is correct and useful for discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission and read messages before finalizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Before final 'Submit Article' step, check both the title/abstract (metadata) and the processed files carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see errors or are unhappy with formatting, correct them or contact arXiv administrators if you cannot resolve problems. If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement, use the Unsubmit icon next to the submission on your user page to return it to incomplete status, allowing modification and later resubmission. Unsubmitting removes the article from the processing queue; announcement will be scheduled based on later resubmission time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing, replacement and versioning rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits before an article is publicly announced will not generate additional versions; the date stamp is the time the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO NOT make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum; replace the original submission. Edits and final submission before 16:00 US Eastern time Monday–Friday will not delay announcement. Edits are permitted between 16:00 and the 20:00 announcement time, but doing this will remove the submission from that day's announcements and delay it until the next day. An edit and subsequent 'Submit' will reset the submission time and change position in the listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility and third-party submission guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make their own submissions; third-party submissions (e.g., by secretaries) are discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions often cause the most problems, presumably due to lack of self-interest and related factors. Ensure institutional affiliation for the author(s) is provided and official report number(s) from the author(s)' institutions are provided as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: All official versions are publicly available
rubrics_metrics.description: All official versions of submitted articles are made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the discussion of submission version availability; be aware that every official submission/version will be accessible publicly and archived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement schedule and listing order
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to arXiv are normally announced on a daily schedule (no activity scheduled on weekends); submissions are assigned identifiers and appear in listings in order based on the submission time (the last time the 'Submit' button was selected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: submissions before 16:00 US Eastern Monday–Friday are typically available after 20:00 same day and appear in next mailing; Friday before 16:00 appears after 20:00 Sunday, etc. Policy change 2010-03 affects announcement order and edits. Be aware that edits reset submission time and can change position in listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard LaTeX macro packages for figure inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv administration cannot provide help with TeX-related issues, so seek help from colleagues if necessary.
